item.title: 5.0.5-beta.1
item.description:
ExtraDock 5.0.5-beta.1 – An Honest Deep-Hide, And The Evidence To Prove It! 🔍🖥️

This is a diagnostic beta. The native-Dock deep-hide is now hardened and, more importantly, honest about what macOS will and won't let it do — and it finally collects the evidence we need to chase the remaining edge case.

✨ Improvements

  • The setting now tells the truth: Hide native macOS Dock is now Deep-hide native macOS Dock, and it says plainly that macOS can still reveal its own Dock at the physical screen edge or in Mission Control!
  • A stubborn Dock gets one polite retry: If the preferences apply but the Dock refuses to reload, ExtraDock makes a single bounded retry instead of rewriting keys or spinning up a restart loop!
  • Deep-hide survives a Dock restart: When macOS replaces the Dock process, suppression is re-applied automatically — and when deep-hide is off, your own Dock settings are never touched!
  • Much richer support exports: All Docks Diagnostics now captures live Dock preferences, the last apply and retry result, Dock process identity, on-screen Dock window geometry, screen frames, and where your pointer was relative to the edge. Window titles are never collected!

🧪 What We Need You To Test

  • Turn on Deep-hide native macOS Dock and restart ExtraDock, then try to coax the system Dock out at the physical screen edge — once slowly, once with a fast flick!
  • Try it on every edge you use: bottom, left, and right, and with more than one display attached if you have them!
  • Check Mission Control too — note whether the Dock appears there!
  • If it escapes, export All Docks Diagnostics immediately and send it over with your macOS build, which edge the Dock is on, and your display layout. That export is what turns this from a hunch into a fix!

🔒 Deliberately Not Shipped

  • No private APIs, no cursor-triggered Dock restarts, no guessed reveal-zone geometry: We'd rather measure the real behavior first than ship a hack that breaks in a future macOS!

🚀 What's Next?

Your results from the edge-approach matrix decide whether a physical-edge mitigation is even possible. Until that evidence is in, the deep-hide bug stays open on purpose!

Thank you for helping test ExtraDock 5! Your feedback drives every improvement we make. 💙

ExtraDock 5.0.4 – Docks That Stay Where You Put Them! 🖥️✨

Everything from the 5.0.4 beta rounds, now stable — plus two fresh fixes.

🐞 Bug Fixes

  • Quitting an app no longer freezes ExtraDock: Choosing Quit from a dock icon's menu could leave the dock and menu bar unresponsive if the app was slow to close — clicks would fall straight through to the desktop!
  • Two identical monitors are told apart: Two displays of the same make and model used to share one identity, so docks landed on the wrong panel — each screen now keeps its own assignment through sleep, wake, and replugging!
  • Keyboard shortcuts work with auto-hide: Using a shortcut on a dock set to hide automatically could lock it out of its edge reveal for good — the shortcut is now a temporary peek that hands control straight back!
  • DockFlow profiles play nice with auto-hide: Switching profiles no longer pins docks open, and restored docks stay revealable!
  • Live widgets grow instead of squeezing: Your 1–4 cell choice is a minimum now — a widget claims extra space whenever its visible tiles need it!
  • No more mystery red capsule: iPhone Mirroring and Handoff no longer get drawn as a stretched notification badge!

✨ Improvements

  • Better support logs: Saving diagnostics now captures the last five hours of activity instead of just the current session, so reporting a problem gets it fixed faster!
  • A proper app name: ExtraDock now shows its full name everywhere macOS asks for it!

🚀 What's Next?

We're always working on making ExtraDock more powerful and intuitive! More features and improvements are on the way based on your feedback!

Thank you for being part of the ExtraDock community! Your feedback drives every improvement we make.
